subject: Understanding the difference in standard deviation of CpGs covered

messages.author: 790e074c50910616
messages.subject: Understanding the difference in standard deviation of CpGs covered
parts:
Hi Altuna,

I am using MethylKit to understand the methylation signature in my samples that are derived from cell-free DNA. In my methylation analysis, I ran only the CpG from the overall CX report that bismark generates. I ran this piece of code to understand the std. deviation of the covered CpG
library(methylKit)

file.list=list('ALS1_792_hg19/ALS1_CG_report.txt',
                 'ALS3_793_hg19/ALS3_CG_report.txt',
                 'ALS4_794_hg19/ALS4_CG_report.txt',
                 'ALS6_798_hg19/ALS6_CG_report.txt',
                 'ALS7_797_hg19/ALS7_CG_report.txt',
                 'ALS8_799_hg19/ALS8_CG_report.txt',
                 'ACRI22_795_hg19/ACRI22_CG_report.txt',
                 'ACRI247_796_hg19/ACRI247_CG_report.txt',
                 'Prost018_791_hg19/Prost018_CG_report.txt'
)

myobj2 = methRead(location = file.list, sample.id = list("ALS1","ALS3","ALS4","ALS6", "ALS7", "ALS8", "ACRI22", "ACRI247", "Prost018"), 
                  assembly = "hg19", dbtype = "tabix", pipeline = "bismarkCytosineReport",
                  header = FALSE, skip = 0, sep = "\t", resolution = "base", 
                  treatment = c(1,1,1,1,1,1,0,0,0), dbdir = "ALS_methyl_call", mincov = 5)
meth=methylKit::unite(myobj2)
pm=percMethylation(meth)
mds=matrixStats::rowSds(pm)
hist(mds,col="cornflowerblue",xlab="Std. dev. per CpG")
the graph I got is this:


then I changed my min.cov value to 10 and also added min.per.group=1L and then again made std.dev.histo:


#this will add those rows in my object, in which from at least one sample, there are Cs/Ts with coverage of 10
meth.min=unite(myobj,min.per.group=1L)



I expected the second histogram should have had more frequency as I took into account those CpG calls where I get at least one sample having Cs/Ts with minCov10? Please correct me if I am wrong. I am confused because the number of hyper/hypo methylated CpG sites that were produced while using the min.cov=5 and normally making the object like this, meth=methylKit::unite(myobj2) (number of records in meth = 1923375) has generated 922 and 450 CpG sites respectively. Whereas the hyper/hypo methylated CpG sites produced after doing stringency of min.cov=10 but adding meth.min=unite(myobj,min.per.group=1L) (number of records in meth.min= 7054146) has generated 4316 and 3261 sites respectively.  I counted these sites from the file that have knowledge of CpGs for "distance from TSS" that I wrote after using the function, getAssociationWithTSS. The obtained numbers of sites are calculated from the unique number of genes names in the "distance from TSS" file. 


I hope my question made a little sense. I wanted to understand why the ultimate number of CpGs is more despite the fact that frequency in the second histogram is less.


I would appreciate your help.


Shruti

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Understanding the difference in standard deviation of CpGs covered
parts:
Hi Shruti,

I guess you get a higher number of Cpg sites in the second case because you set the min.per.group argument to 1L for unite, which is less stringent than our default of requiring that a site has to be covered by all samples.

Best,
Alex

the graph I got is this:


then I changed my min.cov value to 10 and also added min.per.group=1L and then again made std.dev.histo:


#this will add those rows in my object, in which from at least one sample, there are Cs/Ts with coverage of 10
meth.min=unite(myobj,min.per.group=1L)



I expected the second histogram should have had more frequency as I took into account those CpG calls where I get at least one sample having Cs/Ts with minCov10? Please correct me if I am wrong. I am confused because the number of hyper/hypo methylated CpG sites that were produced while using the min.cov=5 and normally making the object like this, meth=methylKit::unite(myobj2) (number of records in meth = 1923375) has generated 922 and 450 CpG sites respectively. Whereas the hyper/hypo methylated CpG sites produced after doing stringency of min.cov=10 but adding meth.min=unite(myobj,min.per.group=1L) (number of records in meth.min= 7054146) has generated 4316 and 3261 sites respectively.  I counted these sites from the file that have knowledge of CpGs for "distance from TSS" that I wrote after using the function, getAssociationWithTSS. The obtained numbers of sites are calculated from the unique number of genes names in the "distance from TSS" file.
